chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd and Muḥammad ibn Khālid, from al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd, from Ibn Miskān, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about the ghusl (ritual bath) of the deceased, so he said: “Wash him with water and lotus leaves, then after that wash him a second washing with water and camphor and dharīrah, if it is available, and wash him the third time with plain water.”
I said: Three washings for his entire body? He said: “Yes.”
I said: Should there be a garment upon him when he is washed? He said: “If you are able, let a shirt be upon him, and wash him from underneath it.”
And he said: “I like that the one who washes the deceased should wrap a cloth around his hand while washing him.”

key_terms.الْخِرْقَةَ: a cloth wrapped around the washer’s hand
key_terms.ذَرِيرَةٍ: a fragrant substance added if available
key_terms.سِدْرٍ: lotus leaves used in the first washing
key_terms.غُسْلِ الْمَيِّتِ: the ritual washing of the deceased body
key_terms.قَمِيصٌ: a shirt placed on the deceased while washing
key_terms.كَافُورٍ: camphor used in the second washing
key_terms.مَاءٍ قَرَاحٍ: plain, unmixed water used in the final washing

ai.seo_question: How should the deceased be washed according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out the legal procedure for the ghusl (ritual bath) of the deceased: three washings, first with water and lotus leaves, second with water and camphor and dharīrah if available, and third with plain water. It also states that the deceased should preferably be washed while wearing a shirt, and that the washer should wrap a cloth around his hand during the washing.
